overall_summary: The channel's performance is heavily driven by extreme cosmic anomalies and exotic exoplanets, which consistently generate the highest views and engagement. Conversely, internal cognitive psychology, brain hacks, and repetitive re-uploads of low-performing concepts fail to capture audience interest. Transitioning to longer, highly visual, and sensory-driven space storytelling (19-21 seconds) yields significantly better retention and reach.

winning_patterns.evidence: The Planet of Burning Ice (1,055 views), TrES-2b: The Planet Darker Than Coal (1,014 views), and the Supersonic Rubies planet (721 views) dominate the top tier of performance.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme exoplanets, focusing on hostile environments, bizarre weather, and visual-first cosmic anomalies.

winning_patterns.evidence: What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like? (368 views) and The Largest Ocean in Space (460 views) outperform standard space facts by linking abstract science to human senses.
winning_patterns.action: Frame cosmic facts using sensory hooks (smell, taste, touch, sound) to make the vastness of space feel tangible.

weak_patterns.evidence: Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories (5-11 views across multiple uploads) and Your Brain Is Hiding This From You (38 views) consistently fail to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from cognitive psychology and self-help brain hacks, as the audience clearly prefers external, high-scale cosmic wonders.

weak_patterns.evidence: Re-uploading identical 12-15s videos like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' multiple times yields near-zero growth.
weak_patterns.action: Stop re-uploading underperforming topics; instead, iterate on successful concepts with longer 19-21s durations to allow for better storytelling.

next_video.hook_style: High-stakes cosmic doom combined with bizarre physical deformation
next_video.concept: WASP-12b, the egg-shaped planet being actively devoured by its host star.
next_video.opening_direction: Right now, this pitch-black planet is literally being eaten alive.
next_video.twist_direction: The star's gravity is pulling the planet so hard it has deformed into a giant egg, and it only has a few million years left before it is completely swallowed.
next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful extreme exoplanet theme with a strong visual hook (egg-shaped planet) and high-stakes cosmic doom, matching the 20-second sweet spot of our top-performing videos.

experiment: Test a 'What-If' style comparative format where we compare the most hostile planet in the universe to Earth's worst environments, measuring if comparative scale increases viewer retention over single-planet showcases.
